verification: Every component below was read from src/index.ts (312 lines), public/index.html (821 lines), package.json and wrangler.json. Line references are exact.

maturityVocabulary.adequate: Works, minor gaps that do not block beta
maturityVocabulary.fragile: Works but a known defect makes it likely to break or mislead

components.name: Cloudflare Workers runtime
components.role: Hosts the app; serves static assets host-side and forwards everything else to the Durable Object
components.notes: html_handling=auto-trailing-slash + not_found_handling=single-page-application configured correctly for an SPA.

components.name: App Durable Object
components.role: Single DO class named App - acts as both the HTTP server and the stateful persistence unit. One instance per (space, branch).
components.entry: src/index.ts:4 export class App extends DurableObject
components.notes: Correct platform pattern - no export default {fetch}, no illegal DO bindings. Constructor does real work (initDb + seedDefaults) on every instantiation, which is a latency and ordering concern.

components.name: Hono router
components.role: In-process HTTP router; 8 routes registered in the DO constructor
components.notes: No 404 fallback route - unknown paths fall through to the assets layer and return the SPA shell, which masks client-side routing errors.

components.name: SQLite storage (DO-attached)
components.role: Per-(space,branch) SQLite database via this.ctx.storage.sql. Two tables: todos (13 cols), lists (5 cols).
components.notes: Schema created idempotently (IF NOT EXISTS) - good. But: tags stored as JSON TEXT (not normalised), no indexes defined beyond PRIMARY KEY, no migration path, and no foreign key from todos.list_id to lists.id.

components.name: Static asset layer
components.role: Serves public/index.html and public/style.css host-side before any Worker invocation
components.notes: The entire 40KB SPA is one HTML file - no code splitting, no caching differentiation between shell and logic.

components.name: Single-file React SPA
components.role: One App() component holding all 24 useState hooks; all UI, data fetching, and timer logic in one scope
components.notes: No component decomposition, no router, no state management boundary. At 821 lines in one function it is at the limit of maintainability; every feature added increases coupling. This is the main structural debt.

components.name: Client-side data access layer
components.role: Six fetch() helpers (fetchTodos, fetchLists, fetchStats, create, patch, delete) calling the relative ./api/* routes
components.notes: All 6 have try/catch that only console.error - no retry, no user feedback, no loading state, no optimistic update. Relative ./api paths are correct for the preview prefix, which is a genuinely good call.

components.name: In-browser JSX transpilation
components.role: Babel standalone compiles the JSX at page load from a type=text/babel script tag
components.notes: No build step - the browser transpiles 40KB of JSX on every load. Adds a visible white-screen delay, requires the react/jsx-runtime importmap entry to be correct (it is), and executes an unpinned third-party script with full page privilege.

components.name: Tailwind Play CDN
components.role: Runtime Tailwind JIT in the browser with an inline tailwind.config (brand palette, darkMode:class, Inter/JetBrains Mono)
components.notes: Vendor explicitly marks this CDN as not-for-production. Unpinned, render-blocking, and duplicates work with COMP-010.

components.name: Custom design tokens
components.role: Brand colour scale as CSS custom properties plus fadeIn/scaleIn keyframes
components.notes: Clean token scale. Note the brand palette is defined TWICE - here as CSS vars and again in the inline Tailwind config at index.html:19-25 - so they can drift.

components.name: Importmap module resolution
components.role: Maps react, react/jsx-runtime, react-dom, react-dom/client and lucide-react to esm.sh with ?external=react,react-dom
components.notes: Correctly applies ?external to every React-consuming package - this is the exact fix for the dual-React/useContext crash, and it is applied consistently. Genuinely well done. Residual risk is CDN availability and absence of SRI.

components.name: Web typography
components.role: Inter (sans) + JetBrains Mono (mono) loaded from Google Fonts with preconnect
components.notes: preconnect with crossorigin is correct. External font CSS can be blocked in privacy-strict regions, and there is no font-display:swap fallback guaranteeing text visibility.

components.name: Server-side seed data
components.role: Injects 4 lists and 4 sample tasks on first run when the lists table is empty
components.notes: Guarded by an empty-table check so it is not destructive, but it cannot be disabled - every deployment starts polluted with demo content and no tester can get a clean slate.

components.name: Configuration & typing
components.role: wrangler.json for deploy; env typed as any in the DO constructor
components.notes: env: any forfeits all binding type safety. No .dev.vars handling, no environment separation, no TypeScript config in the project itself (types come from the platform).

components.name: Quality assurance
components.notes: Nothing verifies any of the 30 features. Any refactor is unguarded. This is the single largest structural gap between alpha and beta.

components.name: Authentication & tenancy
components.role: Identity, access control, data isolation between users
components.evidence: grep for auth|bearer|token|session|cookie = only a string literal in an alert()
components.notes: Isolation currently relies entirely on the platform fact that one DO instance serves one deployment. That is single-tenant by architecture, not by access control - it protects a private deploy but cannot support a shared beta.

dataFlow: Hono [COMP-003] -> SQL exec on DO storage [COMP-004]
DO [COMP-002] persists via ctx.storage.sql, surviving redeploys
Static assets [COMP-005] served host-side; only unmatched requests reach the DO
Third-party CDNs [COMP-008, COMP-009, COMP-011, COMP-012] load at page view, outside the Worker boundary

structuralDebt: COMP-006 - 821 lines, one component, no decomposition
COMP-008/COMP-009 - no build step; runtime transpilation and runtime CSS JIT
COMP-015/COMP-016 - no tests and no auth
summary.assessment: The architecture is coherent and uses the platform correctly - the DO/SQLite/Hono pattern is idiomatic, the importmap is handled with real care, and the asset routing is right. What holds it at alpha is not structural wrongness but three absences (auth, tests, a build step) plus a single-component frontend that cannot absorb much more growth without decomposition.
